ai.description: This lizard reaches 10 cm in length. It features a dark, mottled body with a vibrant orange labial stripe. A distinctive, enlarged rostral scale distinguishes this rare forest dweller.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Microauris aurantolabium* is its distinct, vibrant orange-colored lips, which clearly contrast with its otherwise greenish body.
ai.habitat: *Microauris aurantolabium* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Orange-lipped Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects among leaf litter and low-hanging vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microauris aurantolabium* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microauris aurantolabium* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation shola forests and grasslands in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
